messages:
david.l: Not sure if folks saw this - a handful of customers got failed SCIM syncs this morning. Provisioner returning 403; KMS reports DecryptError in logs.
emily: Any recent changes to OIDC/SAML attribute transforms?
david.l: We rolled an OIDC mapping change last night: `sub -> concat(tenant, ":", user_id)` (was email previously). I suspect extId normalization mismatch.
frank: Can you paste the error snippet?
david.l: `2026-03-23T07:12:14Z provisioner ERROR: KMSDecryptFailed key_ref="" user="svc_scim_007" err="invalid_envelope"`
frank: Blank key_ref is a red flag. Provisioner should look up KMS envelope by external_id. If external_id changed format, the lookup returns nil and decrypt is attempted with empty ref -> invalid_envelope.
platform-sre: Which customers affected? I see 6 orgs with spikes in SCIM failures.
emily: Running query to list recent failures: ```sql
SELECT org, user_email, error FROM scim_provisioning_logs WHERE error LIKE '%KMSDecrypt%'
AND created_at > now() - interval '6 hours';
```
emily: Returns entries for orgs: orchard-co, mesa-labs, coreapi-inc.
david.l: Example SCIM create payload we received: `{"externalId": "orchard:42", "userName": "chris@orchard.co"}`
frank: Our KMS metadata table keys are stored using `tenant/user` format. So `orchard:42` -> lookup miss.
david.l: Where did `:` come from? The OIDC change. We concatenated with `:` to match internal id. Old consumers used `/`.
emily: Why wasn't this caught in integration tests? The OIDC mapping change had unit tests but not contract tests with provisioner.
platform-sre: Immediate mitigation options: 1) Patch provisioner to accept either separator (':' or '/') for 24hrs. 2) Revert OIDC mapping in idp config. 3) Run a migration to backfill KMS metadata keys for new extid format. Revert is risky during day. Patch + migration seems safest.
frank: Do we need to rewrap KMS envelopes? If keys exist only under old ref we can copy metadata entries pointing to same envelope_id under new ref; no cryptographic operations required. But ensure we only create pointers after verifying audit.
david.l: I'll open a quick migration job that scans users with `:` in externalId and creates mapping entries for `tenant/user` variant pointing to the same envelope_id. Add an idempotency guard.
emily: Before we mass-run: add extra logging in provisioner to emit both incoming extid and resolved metadata id (no raw ciphertext). Minimal PII, just hashes.
platform-sre: I'll suppress the SCIM alert group for 2 hours while we run canary migrations so oncall doesn't page.
kms-bot: Actioned: Suppression applied to alert: scim-kms-decrypt-failures for 2h.
frank: Also check audit linking. If we create mapping copies we must annotate them with original audit_event_id so downstream replay is possible.
david.l: Good call. Migration job will attach field `migration_source_event` with the rename event ids.
emily: Canary results: migrated 20 users across orchard-co -> all success, provisioning retried -> success. No new KMS decrypt errors on staging.
frank: Next steps: 1) Deploy provisioner tolerant patch to prod (accept both separators + improved logs), 2) Run full migration with rate limiting and audit annotations, 3) After 48h confirm no further misses, then plan for a single canonical extid format and schedule removal of tolerance shim.
platform-sre: Create a Jira: ENGSEC-1801 - "OIDC extId separator change caused SCIM KMS lookup failures" with rollback/playbook/migration steps.
david.l: Logged and assigned. Runbook draft: https://confluence.internal/redwood/engsec/oidc-scim-backfill.
emily: Postmortem notes for follow-up: - Add contract tests between idp mappings and scim provisioner - Add KMS metadata existence check early in provisioner to fail fast and emit clear audit event - Improve deploy checklist for identity mapping changes.
frank: Marking thread for handoff to infra for full-prod run. Will monitor for 4 hours after migration. :eyes:
